correctness.rationale: Conics are projectively equivalent over F5. On XZ=Y², external lines have normalized A=1 and discriminant 2 or 3, giving ten. Independent enumeration using direct chord equations and incidence tests reproduced all 60 certified images, including distinct collinear opposite-side intersections, and all ten exterior lines. Orbit expansion using translation, scaling by 2 and inversion (generators by the fractional-linear normal form) gave the stated representatives, orbit sizes 30,20,10, and per-line orbit counts 3,2,1. The incidence histogram is 6,15,10 at multiplicities 0,2,3. Distinct linear tangents make the rational multiple points ordinary; every pair meets in the same rational point after extension. The reduced union therefore has 10(Q+1)−15−2·10=10Q−25 points and its complement Q²−9Q+26. Exponentiating the counts yields both stated zeta functions.
residual_risks: Combinatorial fiber size is not scheme-theoretic multiplicity. The zeta computations concern the reduced divisor, and the hexagons use the complete rational six-set.

A distinct indexed general finite-field fiber result covers the exterior-only assertion at q=5 and implies aggregate sixfold fibers by equivariance and the 60 inputs. Its available statement does not determine the decomposition of each fiber into the 30-, 20-, and 10-element domain orbits. That refinement is independently proved and not covered by the strongest accessible comparisons.

value.rationale: The full rational six-set is the smallest complete conic configuration admitting a Pascal hexagon. The split of a single image fiber into three distinct symmetry strata is useful exact information on this finite-field degeneration and is not recoverable from a uniform total or the incidence geometry. The reduced-divisor zeta formula is a useful derived description, not a separate novelty claim.
residual_risks: No assertion about a scheme-theoretic degeneration or arbitrary sextuples in characteristic five.
